data.description:
# Cache redundant whole-tree AST parsing across test scanners

## Context / Problem
Many regression-oracle tests independently walk a source tree (tests/ or src/rebar), read every
*.py, and ast.parse it. Measured: one full parse of tests/ (~1653 files) costs ~2.3s idle
(~7.6s under load) and src/rebar (~597 files) ~0.8s; dozens of test files each repeat such a
walk. The redundant PARSE is ~75-80% of each scan's cost (parse+read vs ast.walk). Under `--cov`
on the coverage cell these scanners are the top `--durations` entries (18.7-29.93s each). After
the macOS cell is reduced (sibling story omphacite-desertlike-coney, 3ba8-49d5-fee5-445d), the
Ubuntu coverage cell becomes the gate's long pole, so cutting this redundancy directly cuts the
gate.

## Approach
Add a shared, process-global memoised parse — tests/_tree_scan.py exposing
`parsed_python_files(root)` returning parsed modules, cached via functools.cache with the root
`.resolve()`d so different spellings share one cache entry. Migrate the whole-tree AST scanners
to it so the FIRST scanner per xdist worker parses a given root and every other scanner reuses it
for free. This is behaviour-preserving: identical file set, identical ASTs; only the walk/read/
parse mechanics are shared. Cross-file proof (prototype, already validated): after migrating the
three heaviest tests-tree scanners the 2nd/3rd scanner dropped 6.64s->2.89s and 5.07s->1.91s with
identical pass/fail. This fits the goal — pure redundancy removal, no test weakened.

## Scope
- tests/_tree_scan.py (NEW) — the cached `parsed_python_files(root)` helper and a `ParsedModule`
  value (path / relative / source / tree).
- Whole-tree `.py` AST scanners under tests/unit/, tests/unit/store/, tests/unit/commands/,
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/, and tests/interfaces/contracts/ — migrate each scanner that does
  `for p in ROOT.rglob("*.py"): ast.parse(p.read_text())` to the shared helper, preserving every
  per-file filter and the exact `relative_to(BASE)` base. Non-`.py` globs (`rglob("*")`, `*.sh`,
  `*.json`) and filename-only collections are left unchanged.

## Testing
- Each migrated file's tests pass unchanged (same selection, same assertions) via
  `pytest <file> -p no:xdist`.
- The full unit tier passes (the scanners' home tier): `pytest tests/unit -m "not integration
  and not external"`.
- Aggregate: the migrated scanner set shows reduced call-time when run in one process (cache
  shared) with identical pass/fail — the redundancy-removal proof.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] tests/_tree_scan.py provides `parsed_python_files(root)` returning parsed modules, memoised
      per process (verified by a same-object second-call check and by the migrated tests passing).
- [ ] The whole-tree AST scanners in Scope call the shared helper; each migrated file passes
      `pytest <file> -p no:xdist` unchanged.
- [ ] No behaviour change: `pytest tests/unit -m "not integration and not external"` yields the
      same pass/fail as before (verified locally green).
- [ ] Running the migrated scanner set in a single process parses each root once — a 2nd+
      same-root scanner is materially faster than a cold parse (verified by a timed probe).
- [ ] ruff check + ruff format are clean on all changed files and the complexity baseline check
      passes.
data.title: Cache redundant whole-tree AST parsing across test scanners
